input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects the laws of the State of New York, which is the playbook's preferred governing law. Searches for "arbitration", "jurisdiction", "courts" and "venue" return no dispute-forum provision anywhere in the agreement, so there is no mandatory arbitration (and no foreign seat) and no exclusive venue in HDI's or any other non-accepted jurisdiction — the walk-away scenario is not present, and disputes would default to the courts. The absence of an express exclusive-jurisdiction reference to the state and federal courts in New York County is a missing sub-element of the preferred wording rather than a failure on a material term, so we note it without redlining; if the agreement is otherwise being amended we would add New York County venue for certainty.
